content: Domain adaptation of PTLMs is typically achieved by pretraining on unlabeled target-domain text. Some examples of such models are BioBERT BIBREF2, which was pretrained on the PubMed and/or PubMed Central (PMC) corpora, SciBERT BIBREF5, which was pretrained on papers from SemanticScholar, ClinicalBERT BIBREF6, BIBREF7 and ClinicalXLNet BIBREF8, which were pretrained on clinical patient notes, and AdaptaBERT BIBREF9, which was pretrained on Early Modern English text. In most cases, a domain-adapted PTLM is initialized from a general-domain PTLM (e.g., standard BERT), though BIBREF5 report better results with a model that was pretrained from scratch with a custom wordpiece vocabulary. In this paper, we focus on BioBERT, as its domain adaptation corpora are publicly available.
